channel.title: Mission Control Newsroom
channel.description: Research and opinion on how work moves through services organisations.

item.title: The month-end close is slow because work waits, not accountants
item.description: The month-end close is slow because work waits, not because accountants are slow. Map it as a dependency network and fix the flow before buying close tools.

item.title: AI agents rarely fail at the task. They fail at the hand-off
item.description: AI agents in services operations rarely fail at the task. They stall at hand-offs. The evidence, and a checklist to design each hand-off before you build the agent.

item.title: Process drift: closing the gap between the SOP and the real work
item.description: A practical playbook for finding the gap between documented and real processes, classifying each variant, and closing it without monitoring what people write.

item.title: The cost of rework: the biggest line your P&L never shows
item.description: Rework is the biggest cost most services firms never measure. How to track first pass yield by workflow and put a price on rework without monitoring individuals.

item.title: Automated decisions: Australia's 10 December privacy deadline
item.description: Australia's new privacy rule on automated decisions starts 10 December 2026. What it requires, how UK and US rules compare, and a practical readiness checklist.

item.title: Work about work is a hand-off problem, not a people problem
item.description: Why 'work about work' takes more than half of the knowledge worker's week, why focus campaigns and new tools underdeliver, and how to measure the hand-offs where time really disappears.

item.title: Flow efficiency: the number that explains why simple work takes weeks
item.description: What flow efficiency is, why knowledge work often sits at 5 to 15 per cent, how Little's Law links open work to cycle time, and how services firms can measure and reduce waiting.

item.title: Why automation programs stall, and how to choose your first five
item.description: Why 30 to 50 per cent of RPA projects and most generative AI pilots fail to deliver, why automating non-bottleneck steps rarely pays, and five tests for choosing automations that do.

item.title: How to build an automation business case your CFO will sign
item.description: A practical method for automation ROI: measured volumes, automation rate, adoption ramps, risk adjustment and full-life costs, plus how to separate capacity released from cash realised.

item.title: How to map work without monitoring people
item.description: Workplace surveillance and privacy law for process discovery in Australia (NSW, ACT, Victoria, Privacy Act), the UK (ICO guidance) and the US (New York, California), and seven privacy-first design principles.
